item.title: Novo's Parkinson's Cell Therapy
item.description:
• Summary: Cellular Intelligence has licensed Novo Nordisk’s shelved Parkinson’s disease cell therapy program. The program involves transplanting dopamine-producing neurons derived from stem cells to replace those lost in Parkinson's disease. Novo Nordisk had deprioritized the asset, but Cellular Intelligence plans to advance it into clinical development. The deal highlights continued interest in cell therapy approaches for neurodegenerative disorders.
  • MoAs: Cell therapy: Replacement of dopamine-producing neurons via transplantation of stem cell-derived dopaminergic neurons.
  • Sources: Pharmaceutical Technology

item.title: Medicare Alzheimer's Drugs Leqembi/Kisunla
item.description:
• Summary: Medicare spending on Alzheimer's drugs Leqembi (lecanemab) and Kisunla (donanemab) has been lower than expected, partly due to lower-than-projected uptake and a narrower billing system that has prompted lobbying from manufacturers. The drugs, which slow cognitive decline by clearing amyloid beta, face challenges including limited patient eligibility, infusion requirements, and the need for regular monitoring. Despite initial hype, actual utilization has been modest, leading to lower government outlays than budgeted.
  • MoAs: Lecanemab (Leqembi): Anti-amyloid beta monoclonal antibody, clears soluble amyloid protofibrils. Donanemab (Kisunla): Anti-amyloid beta monoclonal antibody, targets pyroglutamate-modified amyloid beta plaques.
  • Sources: STAT News, STAT News

item.title: Novo's Parkinson's Cell Therapy (Endpoints)
item.description:
• Summary: Novo Nordisk is pursuing a Parkinson's disease cell therapy program, with news that the therapy has found a new home within the company. Separately, GSK is turning to China for a hepatitis B drug, indicating a broader trend of Western pharma tapping into Chinese biotech innovation.
  • MoAs: Cell replacement therapy using dopaminergic neurons derived from stem cells to restore dopamine production in the brains of Parkinson's patients.
  • Sources: Endpoints News

item.title: Medicare Alzheimer's Drugs Estrogen Patch
item.description:
• Summary: The article discusses a shortage of estrogen patches used for treating Alzheimer's disease, and how Medicare's coverage policies for Alzheimer's drugs are affecting patient access. The estrogen patch shortage exacerbates challenges for patients relying on hormone therapy for Alzheimer's. No specific drug names are highlighted.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: Stat News
